transcript: Yesterday, I saw Teeth, a new musical premiering at Playwrights Horizons, based on the movie of the same name. In very basic terms, this is a story of a girl who's wrestling with sexual shame and religious trauma. It starts out just very funny and campy, and becomes more absurd as it goes on, fueled by female rage and a heavy serving of horror-comedy. If you haven't seen the movie and you don't really know what this is about, you are in for a ride. The book is really funny, the performances are passionate, and the score by Anna K Jacobs and Michael R Jackson of a Strange Loop is easily one of the best new scores I've heard in awhile. They were discouraging folks from filming during curtain call, perhaps because it might spoil a couple things, and I suspect, based on the marketing around this project and its high production value that Playwrights Horizons hopes the show can continue somewhere beyond its current run. And I would be in full support of that — this was a really great musical. Currently it is running until mid-April, so definitely put on your radar if you can. With that, another program for my collection.
